claims.question: Does multimodal fusion beat the best single sensor?
claims.basis: Fused IoU 0.834 (test) and 0.757 (Bolivia) against optical 0.845 and 0.802.
claims.limits: Early fusion only; cloudy pixels are excluded from the labels.

claims.question: Does the model generalise to flood events it was not trained on?
claims.basis: Mean IoU drop when an event is held out: Radar (S1) +0.002, Optical (S2) +0.010, Fused (S1+S2) +0.007.
claims.limits: One seed per fold; held-out models train on more chips; other events from the same continent stay in training; no unseen sensor or climate test.

claims.question: Can uncertainty identify where the model should abstain?
claims.basis: Dropping the least confident 10% of pixels cuts the error rate to 53% of its value (Radar (S1), Bolivia), 29% of its value (Optical (S2), Bolivia), 25% of its value (Fused (S1+S2), Bolivia).
claims.limits: Pixel error is dominated by easy land pixels; no chip-level or decision-level test.

claims.question: Does semantic + spatial + temporal + graph retrieval improve geospatial QA?
claims.verdict: supported for the hybrid score; not supported for the graph component
claims.basis: nDCG@10: vector 0.67, spatial 0.53, hybrid 0.79, hybrid + graph 0.79 on 36 queries.
claims.limits: Queries are generated from the corpus; weights are hand-set.

claims.question: Are specialised agents more reliable than one agent or a fixed workflow?
claims.verdict: supported against the fixed pipeline only
claims.basis: 49 questions. Accuracy: TerraCore 0.78, terracore-no-critic 0.78, fixed-pipeline 0.43, llm-agent (llama3:8b) 0.67. TerraCore answers 89% of answerable questions correctly but refuses only 42% of unanswerable ones; the LLM agent refuses 100% but answers 57%. Removing the critic changes accuracy by +0.00.
claims.limits: Questions written by the author of TerraCore's rules; gold facts come from the same store; one LLM (llama3:8b); 49 questions.

claims.question: Does reinforcement learning beat heuristic and optimisation baselines in simulation?
claims.basis: PPO minus lookahead: -0.029 [-0.039, -0.019] on test, -0.024 [-0.041, -0.007] on bolivia.
claims.limits: Simulated; PPO with parameter sharing rather than full MAPPO; 45 training scenarios; no hyperparameter tuning.

claims.question: Does the integrated chain improve decision quality over separate parts?
claims.verdict: partly: perception matters, uncertainty and calibration barely do
claims.basis: Giving the planner the radar ensemble instead of nothing is worth +0.268; the truth adds only +0.017 more. Calibration or uncertainty gave a gain whose interval excludes zero in 2 of 6 cases: radar ensemble, calibrated in 'scarce, no reveal' (+0.002); radar ensemble + uncertainty in 'scarce, no reveal' (+0.002).
claims.limits: Simulated task with smooth, cell-averaged need; errors cost nothing but time.

claims.question: When mistakes cost something, do calibration and uncertainty improve decisions?
claims.verdict: calibration: in some cases; uncertainty: rarely
claims.basis: Harder task, 6 cases (waste cost x split). Calibrating the chance of a dry cell beat taking the map at face value, interval excluding zero, in 2: cost 0.5, test (+0.039); cost 1.0, test (+0.090). Adding ensemble disagreement to that calibration helped in 1: cost 1.0, test (+0.021).
claims.limits: Simulated; calibration is fitted on validation cells and does not transfer to Bolivia; invented cost structure.
